Rashi on Yevamot 32b:10:1.english: A non-priest who ate - [a bird offering killed by] the pinching of the priests.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:10:2.hebrew: חייב שתים - משום זרות ומשום נבילה, דקרבן הנאכל לכהנים זר האוכלו עובר משום "וזר לא יאכל כי קדש הם" (שמות כ״ט:ל״ג), ולאו היינו אזהרה דמעילה, דכל שיש בו שעת היתר לכהנים אין בו מעילה:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:10:2.english: He is liable [on] two [counts] - Because of [the prohibition of] a non-priest [eating sacred food] and because of [the prohibition of] an unslaughtered carcass (neveilah); for [in the case of] an offering that is eaten by priests, a non-priest who eats it transgresses [the verse], "And a non-priest shall not eat [of them], for they are holy" (Exodus 29:33), and this is not the warning against misappropriation of sacred property (me'ilah), because anything that has a period of permissibility to the priests is not subject to me'ilah.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:11:1.english: It was permitted to priests - [This refers to] a bird sin-offering.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:1:1.hebrew: אמר רבי אבהו מודה ר' יוסי באיסור מוסיף - שהוא חל על איסור, כגון איסור אשת אח, דמוסיף הוא: שבתחלה כשנשא זה את אחותה וזו פנויה, נאסרה עליו משום אחות אשה ומותרת לכל אחיו; נשאת לאחד מהן, נאסרה על כולן משום אשת אח, ועכשיו ניתוסף איסור עליה לגבי שאר אחיו, ומגו דחייל שם אשת אח עלה לגבי שאר אחיו שהיתה מותרת להם, חל נמי השם הזה לגבי דידיה, ואע"ג דאסירא עליה וקיימא. אבל אשת איש ונעשית חמותו — מתחלה היתה אסורה לכל העולם משום אשת איש; נשא זה את בתה, אין איסור זה ראוי להוסיף עליה עם אחרים דנימא מגו דחייל עלייהו ליחול נמי עליה דהאי. דחמותו ונעשית אשת איש ודאי איסור מוסיף הוא, שמתחלה אסורה לזה ומותרת לכל העולם, נעשית אשת איש, איתוסף האי שם עלה לגבי כ"ע, ומגו דחייל עלייהו חייל נמי לגבי דהאי. והאי דקאמר רבי יוסי "נידון בחמותו", משום דבמיתות עסקינן, ואי אתה יכול להמיתו בב' מיתות; הואיל ושתיהן עליו, ידון בחמורה, אבל אם היה שוגג, היה חייב ב' חטאות:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:1:1.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi Yosei concedes with regard to an expanded prohibition - That it takes effect upon [an existing] prohibition, such as the prohibition of a brother's wife, which is an expanded [prohibition]: for initially, when this man married her sister while this [woman] was unmarried, she became forbidden to him on account of [being his] wife's sister, yet [remained] permitted to all his brothers; [when] she married one of them, she became forbidden to all of them on account of [being] a brother's wife, and now a prohibition has been added to her with respect to the rest of his brothers, and since the designation of "brother's wife" takes effect upon her with respect to the rest of his brothers, to whom she was [previously] permitted, this designation also takes effect with respect to him, even though she already stands forbidden to him. However, [in the case of] a married woman who became his mother-in-law — initially she was forbidden to the entire world on account of [being] a married woman; [when] this man married her daughter, this prohibition is not fit to add [any new restriction] upon her with respect to others such that we could say, "Since it takes effect upon them, let it also take effect upon this man." For [in the case of] his mother-in-law who became a married woman, it is certainly an expanded prohibition, since initially she was forbidden to this man and permitted to the entire world; [once] she became a married woman, this designation was added upon her with respect to everyone, and since it takes effect upon them, it also takes effect with respect to this man. And that which Rabbi Yosei said, "[He is] judged for [having relations with] his mother-in-law," [is] because we are dealing with [capital] executions, and you cannot execute him with two deaths; since both [punishments] are upon him, he is judged with the more severe one, whereas if he acted unwittingly, he would be liable for two sin-offerings.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:2:1.hebrew: תינח נשא חי - דאחות אשה קדים, ואח"כ נשא מת, אתי איסור אשת אח חייל, כדפרישית, מגו דאיתוסף איסורא דהאי שם לגבי אחיו כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:2:1.english: This works out well [where] the living [brother] married - For [the prohibition of] a wife's sister came first, and afterward the deceased [brother] married [her], [so] the prohibition of a brother's wife comes [and] takes effect, as I explained: since the prohibition of this category was added for his brothers, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:3:1.hebrew: אלא היכא דנשא מת - דאיסור אשת אח קדים עליה דהאי, ואח"כ נשא אחותה, מאי תוספת איכא עלה דקמייתא לגבי אחריני דנימא מגו:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:3:1.english: However, where [the] deceased [brother] married - for the prohibition of a brother's wife preceded [it] upon this [living brother], and afterward he married her sister, what addition [of prohibition] is there upon the first [woman] regarding others, that we should say migo?

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:4:1.hebrew: וכי תימא מגו - דבהנך נישואין דבתרייתא מתסר האי גברא בכולהו אחוותא משום אחות אשה — דעד השתא הוו שריין ליה — איתסר נמי משום האי שמא גופיה עלה דקמייתא שהיא אשת אחיו. האי לאו איסור מוסיף הוא, דהא עלה דקמייתא לא איתוסף איסור לגבי אחרינא, אלא איסור כולל הוא, דכייל לה לקמייתא בשם אחות אשה מגו דחייל על אחותה:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:4:1.english: And if you would say: Since - through this latter marriage this man becomes prohibited to all the sisters on account of [the prohibition of] a wife's sister — for until now they were permitted to him — he also becomes prohibited on account of this very designation with respect to the first [sister], who is his brother's wife; [the Gemara answers:] this is not an expanded prohibition, for with respect to the first [sister] no prohibition was added regarding anyone else. Rather, it is an inclusive prohibition, as it includes the first [sister] under the designation of a wife's sister since [that prohibition] takes effect upon her sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:4:2.hebrew: איסור מוסיף - כשהאיסור מוסיף על החתיכה, לאוסרה על מי שמותרת עליו. איסור כולל — שהאיסור חל על חתיכות אחרות, ואותה גוררת לזו עמהם על ידי מגו:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:4:2.english: An expanded prohibition - When the prohibition adds onto the piece, to prohibit it to someone to whom it [was previously] permitted. An inclusive prohibition — [meaning] that the prohibition takes effect on other pieces, and that [prohibition] drags this one along with them by means of migo ["since"].

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:4:3.hebrew: ואית דגרסי הכא ותו חמותו ונעשית אשת איש איסור מוסיף הוא - ושיבוש הוא בידם, ואע"ג דודאי איסור מוסיף הוא, לאו פירכא היא; דודאי אית ליה לר' יוסי איסור מוסיף — כגון אשת איש — חל על איסור חמותו, ותרוייהו איסורי עליה. והא דקאמר ונידון בחמותו, משום דזו היא החמורה; דאי אמרת נידון באשת איש, אם כן אין זה איסור חל על איסור, אלא איסור מבטל איסור:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:4:3.english: And there are those who read here: "And furthermore, [if she was] his mother-in-law and became a married woman, it is an expanded prohibition" - But it is an error in their hands, [for] even though it is certainly an expanded prohibition, it is not a refutation; for Rabbi Yose certainly holds [that] an expanded prohibition — such as [that of] a married woman — takes effect upon the prohibition of his mother-in-law, and both prohibitions are upon him. And that which he states, "and he is sentenced for [violating the prohibition of] his mother-in-law," is because this is the more severe [prohibition]; for if you say he is sentenced for [a] married woman, if so, this is not a prohibition taking effect upon a prohibition, but rather a prohibition nullifying a prohibition.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:5:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - לעולם לית ליה לר' יוסי איסור חל על איסור, והא דקאמר לעיל "חייב עלה משום אשת אח ומשום אחות אשה", לאו בשוגג לחייבו שתי חטאות, אלא במזיד, וליעשות רשע גמור ולקברו בין רשעים גמורים, שהרשע נקבר אצל רשעים, דתנן בסנהדרין (דף מו.): שתי קברות היו מתוקנין לב"ד, א' לנהרגין ולנחנקין וא' לנסקלין ולנשרפין. והכא נמי, אע"ג דהאי לאו מחייבי ב"ד הוא, הואיל ועבד תרתי, קברינן ליה גבי נסקלין ונשרפין:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:5:1.english: Rather, Rava said - Actually, Rabbi Yosei does not hold [that] a prohibition takes effect upon [another] prohibition, and that which he said above, "he is liable for it on account of a brother's wife and on account of a wife's sister," is not [referring to] an unwitting [transgression] to obligate him [to bring] two sin-offerings, rather [it refers to] a deliberate [transgression], and [means] to become completely wicked and to be buried among the completely wicked, for a wicked person is buried next to [other] wicked people, as we learned in a Mishnah in Sanhedrin (46a): Two burial [places] were prepared for the court — one for those executed by beheading and by strangulation, and one for those executed by stoning and by burning. And here too, even though this [person] is not among those liable [to execution] by the court, since he committed two [transgressions], we bury him with those executed by stoning and by burning.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:6:1.hebrew: חייב ב' - ב' איסורי קחשיב, דהא משום זרות אין כאן חטאת, דהא על זדונו מיתה בידי שמים הוא, ואין חייב חטאת אלא על שגגת כרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:6:1.english: He is liable [for] two - He is counting two prohibitions, for on account of [serving as] a non-priest there is no sin-offering here, since for its intentional [transgression] [the penalty] is death at the hand of Heaven, and one is only liable [for] a sin-offering for an unwitting [transgression punishable by] karet.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:6:2.english: From Rabbi - Our Holy Rabbi [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi].

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:7:1.hebrew: כשהותרה במקדש הותרה - סתם, הלכך אין כאן אלא משום זרות:
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:7:1.english: When it was permitted in the Temple, it was permitted - [It was permitted] without qualification; therefore, there is [a transgression] here only on account of [his being] a non-priest.

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:8:1.hebrew: ששימש בטומאה - בקרבן צבור קאמר שדוחה הטומאה, וכן זר ששימש בשבת. ויש כאן משום טומאה, ואזהרתיה מ"וינזרו מקדשי בני ישראל ולא יחללו" (ויקרא כ״ב:ב׳):
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:8:1.english: Who served while ritually impure - [The Gemara] is speaking of a communal offering, which overrides ritual impurity, and similarly [in the case of] a non-priest who served on Shabbat. And there is [a prohibition] here on account of ritual impurity, and its warning [is derived] from "that they separate themselves from the sacred things of the children of Israel, and that they not profane" (Leviticus 22:2).

Rashi on Yevamot 32b:9:1.hebrew: אצל תמימים הותרה - דראוים לעבוד, דילפינן מבמועדו אפי' בטומאה (פסחים דף עז.):
Rashi on Yevamot 32b:9:1.english: It was permitted for unblemished [priests] - For they are fit to serve, as we derive from "in its appointed time" — even in [a state of] ritual impurity (Pesachim 77a).

Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:4:1.hebrew: איסור כולל הוא - וא"ת: ודלמא ר' יוסי אית ליה נמי איסור כולל? ואומר ר"י דקסבר דאשת איש ונעשית חמותו נמי איסור כולל הוא, דמגו דאיתסר בשאר קרובות, וקתני דנידון באשת איש. ומיהו אר"י דלההוא לישנא דלקמן, דסבר רבי חייא דרבי יוסי מחייב תרתי באיסור כולל, צ"ל דאשת איש ונעשית חמותו לא חשיב איסור כולל אע"ג דאיתסר בשאר קרובות, כיון שאין שם אחד, כי היכי דלא תקשה דרבי יוסי אדר' יוסי. והא דחשיב איסור כולל בעל מום ששימש בטומאה — דמעיקרא שרי באכילה ואסור בעבודה; איטמי ליה, מגו דאיתסר באכילה איתסר נמי בעבודה — אכילה ועבודה חשיב נמי שם אחד, דשניהם נאסרו בלשון קריבה: דבעבודה כתיב: "כל איש אשר בו מום לא יגש להקריב לחם וגו'" (ויקרא כ״א:י״ח), ובאכילה בטומאה כתיב: "איש איש אשר יקרב מכל זרעכם וגו'" (שם כב), דמיירי באכילה, כדאמרינן בפ"ב דמעילה (דף י:) ובזבחים (דף מה:). ומיהו איסור מוסיף, אומר ר"י דחשיב אפילו כשאין השמות שוין, כדמוכח בפ' אמרו לו (כריתות יד:) גבי הבא על בת בתו חייב משום כלתו כו', ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:4:1.english: It is an inclusive prohibition (issur kolel) - And if you will say: perhaps R. Yose also holds of an inclusive prohibition? And R.I. says that [the Gemara] holds that [the case of] a married woman who became his mother-in-law is also an inclusive prohibition, since because he becomes prohibited to [her] other relatives [he also becomes prohibited to her], yet [the Mishnah] teaches that he is judged [only] as [having cohabited with] a married woman. However, R.I. says that according to that version below, where R. Chiyya holds that R. Yose obligates two [offerings] in [a case of] an inclusive prohibition, one must say that a married woman who became his mother-in-law is not considered an inclusive prohibition, even though he becomes prohibited to [her] other relatives, since they do not have one name [i.e., a shared category], so that [one statement of] R. Yose will not contradict [the other statement of] R. Yose. And [as for] that which is considered an inclusive prohibition — a blemished [kohen] who served while impure, where initially he was permitted to eat [sacrificial food] and prohibited from [performing] the Temple service, [and when] he became impure, since he became prohibited from eating, he also became [newly] prohibited from the service — eating and service are also considered one name, because both of them are prohibited with the expression of "approaching": for regarding service it is written: "Any man in whom there is a blemish shall not approach to offer the bread, etc." (Leviticus 21:18), and regarding eating in impurity it is written: "Any man from among all your offspring who approaches, etc." (ibid., [ch.] 22), which refers to eating, as we say in the second chapter of Me'ilah (10b) and in Zevachim (45b). However, an expanded prohibition (issur mosif), R.I. says, is considered [effective] even when the names are not equal, as is proven in the chapter Amru Lo (Keritot 14b) regarding one who cohabits with his daughter's daughter being liable on account of [her being] his daughter-in-law, etc., and there is no need to elaborate here.

Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:4:2.hebrew: ותו חמותו ונעשית אשת איש איסור מוסיף הוא - בקונטרס לא גרס ליה, דאפילו חייל עליה איסור אשת איש — נידון בחמורה. וליכא למימר דמשמע ליה נידון בחמותו ולא חל כלל איסור אשת איש, ואם לא התרו בו משום חמותו אלא משום אשת איש — פטור, דהא בפרק הנשרפים (סנהדרין דף פא. ושם) פריך רב אדא בר אהבה: "וליתרו נמי משום איסור אשת איש, דהא א"ר אבהו: מודה רבי יוסי באיסור מוסיף!" ומשני ליה התם: "אדא ברי, אטו בתרי קטלי קטלת ליה?!" משמע בהדיא דחל איסור אשת איש, אלא משום דנידון בחמורה. ור"ת אומר דשפיר גרס ליה, וטעי הכא כדהוה טעי התם רב אדא בר אהבה, והוה סבור דנידון בחמותו משום דלא חייל עליה איסור אשת איש; ולא חש לתרץ, כיון דע"כ צריך לשינויא אחרינא משום קושיא קמייתא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:4:2.english: "And furthermore, [regarding] his mother-in-law who became a married woman, is it an expanded prohibition?" - In the Kuntres [Rashi], he does not have this reading, for even if the prohibition of a married woman takes effect upon it, he is judged with the more severe [penalty]. And one cannot say that it means to him [that] he is judged as [having cohabited with] his mother-in-law and the prohibition of a married woman did not take effect at all — and [consequently] if they did not warn him on account of his mother-in-law, but rather on account of a married woman, he would be exempt — for in the chapter Hanisrafim (Sanhedrin 81a, and there), Rav Adda bar Ahavah asks: "Let them also warn him on account of the prohibition of a married woman, for Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi Yosei concedes regarding an expanded prohibition!" And it answers him there: "Adda, my son, are you going to execute him with two death penalties?!" This explicitly implies that the prohibition of a married woman did take effect, and it is only because he is judged with the more severe [penalty]. And Rabbeinu Tam says that one properly reads this [text], and [the questioner] erred here just as Rav Adda bar Ahavah erred there, thinking that he is judged as [having cohabited with] his mother-in-law because the prohibition of a married woman does not take effect upon it; and [the Gemara] did not bother to answer [this], since it perforce requires another answer because of the first question.

Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:5:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא מעלה כו' - לפי המסקנא דהכא לא איצטריך לר' אבהו למימר דמודה ר' יוסי באיסור מוסיף; מ"מ בהנשרפים (ג"ז שם) מייתי מדרבי אבהו, משום דהאמת הוא דמודה ר' יוסי באיסור מוסיף, כדמשמע בפ' אמרו לו (כריתות דף יד: ושם) גבי א"ר יוסי: "אם עבר זקן ונשאה, חייב עליה משום אשת אב". משום הכי איצטריך ליה לרבי אבהו לאסוקי הכי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:5:1.english: "Rather, Rava said: I ascribe, etc." - According to the conclusion here, it was not necessary for Rabbi Abahu to say that Rabbi Yosei agrees regarding an expanding prohibition (issur mosif); nevertheless, in [the chapter entitled] HaNisrafim (also there), [the Gemara] cites Rabbi Abahu's [statement], because the truth is that Rabbi Yosei agrees regarding an expanding prohibition, as is implied in the chapter [entitled] Amru Lo (Keritot 14b and [the parallel] there) regarding [where] Rabbi Yosei said: "If an old man transgressed and married her, he is liable for her on account of a [father's] wife." Therefore, it was necessary for Rabbi Abahu to conclude thus:

Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:5:2.hebrew: בין רשעים גמורים - פירוש: אצל רשעים כמותו, לפי שאין קוברין רשע אצל צדיק, ולא כמו שפירש בקונטרס לקוברו אצל נסקלים ונשרפין. ור"ש סבר דאע"פ שיש בעבירה זו שני איסורין, כיון דלא מיחייב אלא חדא, אין קוברין אותו אצל רשעים גמורים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:5:2.english: Among the completely wicked - Explanation: [This means] among wicked people like himself, because one does not bury a wicked person next to a righteous person — and not as Rashi explained, to bury him next to those who are stoned and burned. And Rabbi Shimon holds that even though there are two prohibitions in this transgression, since he is liable for only one, we do not bury him among the completely wicked.

Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:8:1.hebrew: בעל מום ששימש בטומאה - הא דלא נקט זר כדנקט לעיל, היינו משום דאטומאה לא הוזהרו זרים אלא כהנים, דכתיב: "דבר אל אהרן ואל בניו וינזרו וגו'" (ויקרא כ״ב:ב׳). והא דקאמר "טומאה לכל נאסרה" — היינו אפי' בעלי מומין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 32b:8:1.english: A [priest] with a blemish who served while ritually impure - The reason [the Gemara] did not mention a non-priest as it mentioned above is because regarding ritual impurity, non-priests were not warned, only priests, as it is written: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they separate themselves, etc." (Leviticus 22:2). And that which it says, "ritual impurity was forbidden to all" — this means even [to priests] with blemishes.
